title: ScrollArea
summary: A region that scrolls inside a screen is Modifier.verticalScroll or horizontalScroll with a bounded size, or a LazyColumn for long content. Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: For a panel, a log, a code block or a row of items that scrolls inside a screen. Bound it with height or heightIn(max =), and use a LazyColumn when the content is long or made of many items.
whenNotToUse: For the screen itself, make the whole content one scrolling container (a LazyColumn or a Column with verticalScroll) instead of nesting scroll areas. Do not nest a scroll area in another of the same direction without a bounded size.
api: fun Modifier.verticalScroll(state: ScrollState, enabled: Boolean = true, flingBehavior: FlingBehavior? = null, reverseScrolling: Boolean = false): Modifier
fun Modifier.horizontalScroll(state: ScrollState, enabled: Boolean = true, flingBehavior: FlingBehavior? = null, reverseScrolling: Boolean = false): Modifier

states.name: scrollable
states.description: The content is larger than the area: it scrolls and TalkBack offers the scroll actions.

states.name: fits
states.description: The content fits: nothing scrolls and no scroll action is offered.

appearance: No appearance of its own. The overscroll stretch at the ends is the system's. Compose on Android draws no scrollbar for these containers.
platformNotes: The web ScrollArea draws thin themed scrollbars, adds edge shadows and becomes a labelled, focusable region only when it actually scrolls. By default, the scroll indicators are the system's; in Compose on Android, verticalScroll, horizontalScroll and lazy lists draw no scrollbar at all, so nothing needs theming and there is none to show. ScrollState.scrollIndicatorState exposes the offset, content size and viewport size for an app that wants to draw one, and canScrollForward and canScrollBackward replace the web's onScrollableChange. A scroll container needs no focus stop: TalkBack scrolls as it moves through the content and offers scroll actions, and a hardware keyboard scrolls the focused container. The web's height and maxHeight are height and heightIn(max =). iOS uses ScrollView, whose indicators are the system's.
accessibility: System behavior: TalkBack scrolls the container as it moves to elements outside it and offers scroll forward and backward actions while there is more content.
Content that fits does not expose scroll actions.
edgeCases: A scroll area without a bounded size grows to its content and never scrolls.
A LazyColumn inside verticalScroll throws; give the lazy list a fixed height or use it as the only scroller.
